description: AgroSpace is an interactive educational game that uses NASA data to teach sustainable farming practices adapted to African climates. Through storytelling, missions, and challenges, players learn to tackle droughts, climate change, and soil degradation while making decisions about crop selection, water management, and sustainable agriculture.
summary:
AgroCyberSpace is an open-source educational agriculture
    platform designed to empower smallholder farmers,
    agricultural extensionists, and students in Mozambique
    by transforming complex Earth Observation datasets into
    actionable, story-driven farming decisions.

    Smallholder communities face acute climate
    volatility—from Limpopo basin flood and drought cycles
    in Gaza to irregular rainfall in Zambézia and Tete.
    While NASA satellite data is openly available, rural
    communities lack the tools and data science expertise
    required to interpret raw satellite telemetry.

    AgroCyberSpace bridges this gap through two integrated
    components:
    1. AgroSight API: A high-performance Python/FastAPI
    geospatial backend integrating NASA POWER meteorological
    reanalysis, CENACARTA administrative boundaries,
    national crop statistics (INE/MADER CAP 2023/2024), and
    pedological soil maps (INIA 1995) via
    PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
    2. AgroSpace: An accessible, offline-resilient React 19
    web application featuring 12 interactive story chapters,
    voice narration in Portuguese and English, and agronomic
    mini-challenges.

    Instead of unreliable generative hallucinations, the 
    platform provides deterministic agronomic guidance and
    traffic-light indicators for crop rotation, planting 
    windows, and soil conservation, grounding space science
    directly into local field realities.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

AgroCyberSpace translates orbital satellite observations

and national agronomic datasets into an accessible,

interactive educational journey tailored to Mozambican

agro-ecological zones (Gaza, Zambézia, and Tete).

The system consists of two synergistic layers:

  • AgroSight API (Geospatial Backend): Built with

Python 3.12, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL 16 / PostGIS. It

runs an asynchronous ingestion pipeline that collects

and normalizes daily meteorological reanalysis from NASA

POWER, verifies spatial boundaries via CENACARTA 2017

district geometries, and contextualizes them with

national agricultural census data (INE/MADER CAP) and

soil classifications (INIA 1995).

  • AgroSpace Web Application: An offline-first Single

Page Application built on React 19 and TypeScript. It

guides players through 12 story chapters inspired by

participatory storytelling. Farmers and students explore

simulated scenarios—interpreting rainfall onset (NASA

GPM), monitoring surface soil moisture (NASA SMAP),

evaluating vegetation vigor (Landsat NDVI), and planning

multi-year crop rotations.

  • Accessible Voice Engine: Integrates browser-native

speech synthesis (Web Speech API) with Portuguese and

English multi-accent narration, enabling low-literacy

smallholders to listen to dialogues, lessons, and

agronomic explanations.

  1. What benefits does it have?
  • Demystifies Space Technology: Translates gigabytes

of complex satellite reanalysis into intuitive "traffic

light" indicators (Favorable / Caution / Risk) that

farmers can readily act upon.

  • Reduces Crop Failure Risk: Empowers rural

producers to identify erratic rainfall onset, avoid

premature sowing, and mitigate seasonal dry spells.

  • Promotes Biodiversity and Soil Health: Recommends

sustainable crop rotations backed by verified district

presence and nitrogen-fixing legume pairings, avoiding

monoculture soil depletion.

  • Offline Resilience: Rural communities often lose

cellular coverage; AgroSpace caches progression and

chapter content in local storage, allowing seamless

offline learning and decision practice.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Smallholder farming accounts for over 80% of

agricultural production in Mozambique. By democratizing

Earth Observation literacy, AgroCyberSpace aims to:

  • Strengthen climate adaptation for vulnerable farming

families in the Limpopo, Licungo, and Zambezi river

basins.

  • Equip agricultural extension workers (SDAE) and

technical schools with interactive pedagogical tooling.

  • Promote participatory science by encouraging farmers

to cross-validate satellite indicators with

on-the-ground soil and crop observations.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or

software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: Python 3.12, TypeScript,

SQL (PostGIS).

  • Backend & Geospatial: FastAPI, Pydantic v2,

SQLAlchemy 2, GeoAlchemy2, PostGIS, Alembic, Shapely,

Argon2id, PyJWT, uv package manager.

  • Frontend & Web: React 19, Vite, Lucide Icons, Web

Speech API (TTS), LocalStorage API.

  • DevOps & Infrastructure: Docker multi-stage

builds, Docker Compose, Nginx reverse proxy, GitHub

Actions CI/CD workflows, Ruff, Mypy, Oxlint, Pytest.

  • Satellite & Open Data Providers: NASA POWER Daily

API, NASA GPM, NASA SMAP, USGS/NASA Landsat 8/9,

CENACARTA, INE/MADER, INIA/IIAM.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Narrative-Driven Space Agriculture: Instead of

another sterile dashboard of graphs, the platform frames

Earth Observation as an engaging narrative dialogue

between an astronaut and local farmers (such as Dona

Amélia).

  • Deterministic Guidance (Anti-Hallucination):

Recognizing that inaccurate farming advice can cause

severe crop and financial loss, our advisory engine

completely avoids black-box generative AI

hallucinations. Every hint, signal, and explanation is

deterministically generated from scientifically verified

datasets, with explicit source citations, timestamps,

and spatial resolution warnings.

  • Gamified Agronomic Mechanics: Features custom

interactive mini-challenges including rainfall zone

splitters, soil texture ribbon tests, NDVI color scale

interpretation, and multi-season crop rotation boards.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Real Local Agro-Ecologies: Tailored context to

three specific Mozambican provinces: Gaza (semi-arid

Limpopo irrigation, flood/drought risks), Zambézia

(humid Licungo basin, cassava/maize systems), and Tete

(Angónia highland fertile plateaus).

  • Technological & Connectivity Constraints:

Lightweight bundle sizes, low battery/CPU consumption on

mobile browsers, and offline state synchronization.

  • Scientific Honesty & Resolution Limits: We

explicitly distinguish between regional gridded

satellite models (e.g., SMAP ~9 km, NASA POWER ~0.5°)

and parcel-level ground truth, teaching farmers the

boundaries and complementary nature of remote sensing.

  • Language & Cultural Inclusivity: Full Portuguese

localization (Mozambique's official language) and

English, complemented by spoken audio for non-readers.
